finding: The provider-limit pattern matches lines that are not a provider limit, so a crashed headless run gets parked instead of exited.
why: `quota`, a bare `rate limit` and `limit reached` match any of the last 20 lines. Probe: limit_line returns a line for `rate limit hit, retrying` followed by `Traceback: boom` and `Error: ENOENT`, for `Error: context limit reached for this conversation`, and for `wrote quota.py` followed by `error: tests failed`. With a non-zero exit, each of these gives parked with an empty body path. The contact agent then parks the role instead of the stop-and-resume path in SDD §7 "Agent dies mid-work".
fix: Match only provider usage-limit phrases (usage limit, hit your limit, the `|<epoch>` form). Drop bare `quota` and `rate limit`, skip lines that say `retrying`, or read only the last non-blank lines.
evidence: LIMIT = re.compile(r"usage limit|limit reached|hit your (?:usage )?limit|rate[ _-]?limit|quota", re.I)

finding: An ISO 8601 reset time with no zone offset gives a wrong reset time, not none: the clock fallback reads the minutes and seconds as the hour and minute, or drops the date.
why: The ISO pattern requires `Z` or an offset, so the line falls through to `_clock`, and CLOCK_24 matches `15:00` in `T10:15:00` (no word boundary before `10`, a boundary before `15`). Probe with seen_at 2026-09-29T08:00Z: `usage limit reached; resets at 2026-09-29T10:15:00` gives 2026-09-29T19:00Z on this machine, and `resets at 2026-10-02 10:15:00` gives 2026-09-29T14:15Z, 3 days early. The parked body then states a false time, and the contact agent resumes the role before the provider resets (PRD AC-023).
fix: Let the ISO pattern take an optional offset and read an offset-less match as machine-local time, or return None for it before the `_clock` fallback runs.

finding: A reset date with no year, or with a day word such as `tomorrow`, is dropped, and the clock time alone gives a reset time on the wrong day.
why: DATE requires a 4-digit year, so `_clock` treats the line as a time alone and takes its next occurrence after seen_at. Probe with seen_at 2026-09-29T08:00Z: `limit reached, resets Oct 2 at 3pm (UTC)` gives 2026-09-29T15:00Z, not 2026-10-02T15:00Z. `resets at 10:15 tomorrow (UTC)` gives 2026-09-29T10:15Z. The contact agent gets an early, wrong reset time where D-149 says an unreadable time gives an empty body path.
fix: Accept a month and day with no year (take the next occurrence), and return None when the text after `resets` holds a month name or a day word that the parser does not read.
evidence: DATE = re.compile(r"\b(" + "|".join(MONTHS) + r")[a-z]*\.?\s+(\d{1,2})(?:st|nd|rd|th)?,?\s+(\d{4})\b", re.I) ... else: day = base.replace(tzinfo=None, hour=hour, minute=minute, second=0, microsecond=0)

finding: The counter test proves only the processed folder; ids in inbox and bodies are not shown to raise the counter (D-151)
why: Sampled mutations that drop `inbox` or `bodies` from the scanned folders both left all 38 tests green, because processed holds a1-sup-4, which is above the bodies id a1-sup-2, and the inbox file a1-7.json does not match.
fix: Add one case per folder where that folder alone holds the highest a1-sup-<n>, and assert the next id is one above it.
evidence: `for folder in ("inbox", "processed", "bodies"):`; test lines 120-126 fixture `("processed", "a1-sup-4.json"), ("bodies", "a1-sup-2"), ("inbox", "a1-7.json")`; mutants M6, M7 SURVIVED

finding: No test holds a claim whose holder state is 'unknown', so narrowing the refusal to 'same' survives
why: Sampled mutation `!= "gone"` -> `== "same"` left all 38 tests green, so a live holder with no readable start time could start a second supervisor (SDD §6 invariant I20) without a failing test.

finding: The handle-only watch path has no test where agent-status answers alive, so dropping the alive check survives
why: Sampled mutation `return code == 0 and status.get("alive") is False` -> `return code == 0` left all 38 tests green: no test proves the supervisor keeps waiting while a handle-only agent is alive.
fix: Add a case where the stand-in answers alive True for N polls, then False, and assert nothing is sent before the flip.
evidence: mutant M3 SURVIVED | 38 passed; the only handle test stubs `"alive": False` (test lines 44 and 367-371)

finding: ended() hands out a finished process id with no started_at, so a reused id makes the supervise loop wait for ever
why: Team.agent records pid without started_at, so when Windows reuses the id, entry._same_process answers 'unknown' (not 'gone') and supervise_agent polls with no deadline; the journal records one run of this file that did not finish in 120 s (inferred cause, not reproduced), and the agent-start test then leaves a detached supervisor running.
fix: Record a started_at that cannot match a new process (e.g. the ended process's creation time read before it exits, or a fixed past ISO time as the claim test does at line 310), and give the tests a loop deadline.
evidence: test line 51: `**({"pid": pid, "handle": str(pid)} if pid else {})` (no started_at); entry.py _same_process: `if started_at in (None, ""): return "unknown"`; JOURNAL.md:472 `one early run of the test file did not finish in 120 s and was stopped`

criterion: blast radius: a downstream contract the diff changed but did not update
finding: The slice adds a new run-directory folder `<run>/supervisors/<agent-id>/` (claim files that are never deleted, plus each parked body's source .txt at line 259), but the cleanup contract that deletes run files does not list it.
why: Plan D-150 says 'cleanup removes them with the run folder', but cleanup step 2 deletes only an enumerated message area and steps 4-5 delete named files, so no pending subtask is bound to remove this folder and it outlives the run.
fix: Have the human add `supervisors/` to 0012-cleanup's step-2 Acceptance bullet, or record a wiring IOU anchored to 0012-cleanup `def run_cleanup(` that names this folder.
evidence: supervisor.py:84 `folder = run_dir / "supervisors" / agent_id`; DECISIONS.md D-150 'claim files are never deleted ... and cleanup removes them with the run folder'; plan/0012-cleanup.md:27 'Steps 2 to 5 delete the message area of the run directory (message bodies, inboxes with their processed folders, completion signals and result files in the run directory), then the knowledge store, then the resolved pattern, then the manifest, last'; SDD §7 E6 step 2 has the same enumeration

finding: In the window D-150 names, the second supervisor's exit 2 reaches no caller: agent-start already answered 0 with its process id.
why: Acceptance says a second supervisor for one agent is refused at start with exit 2, naming the agent. Here the refusal goes to a discarded output stream, so the contact agent writes a process entry for a supervisor that has ended and never sees the refusal.
fix: Make agent-start wait for the child's claim (for example, a short check that the child holds a claim file or is still alive) and answer exit 2 with the child's reason when it refused; or record in D-150 that in this window the refusal is silent and the starter gets exit 0.
evidence: supervisor.py:93 `raise Refused(f"agent {agent_id} already has a job supervisor, process {held['pid']}")`; entry.py:408 `stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL` then `return 0, {"pid": child.pid, "label": label}`; contract Acceptance: "a second supervisor for one agent is refused at start with exit 2, naming the agent (SDD §6)"; D-150: "two starts inside that window both pass the manifest check"

finding: No 12 am or 12 pm reset time is tested, so dropping `% 12` survives
why: Sampled mutation `hour % 12 + ...` -> `hour + ...` left all 38 tests green, so `resets 12am` would read as noon and `12pm` would be refused, with no failing test.
evidence: `hour = hour % 12 + (12 if twelve.group(3).lower() == "p" else 0)`; test parametrize rows use only 10:15am, 7am and 3:05 PM; mutant M5 SURVIVED

finding: A poll that lands between the headless agent's exit and the job owner's status write reads exit_code as unknown, so an exit-0 run whose log names a limit gets parked.
why: `_ended` sees the process gone as soon as the harness exits. The job owner writes exit_code only after `child.wait()` returns (adapters/transport/headless/job.py:96-97), so agent-status answers `exit_code: None` in that window, and `_verdict` treats None as non-zero.
fix: When agent-status answers exit_code None, poll the status again for a few seconds before you read the log.
evidence: if code == 0 and status.get("exit_code") == 0: return "exited", None, None   |   job.py:96 code = child.wait()  job.py:97 _write(status, {**state, "exit_code": code})

finding: No test pins that a relative reset time counts from the log's last write
why: Sampled mutation `reset_time(line, tail[1])` -> `reset_time(line, datetime.now(timezone.utc))` left all 38 tests green; the end-to-end parked test uses only the epoch form, which ignores seen_at.
fix: Add an end-to-end parked case with `try again in 2 hours`, set the log mtime with os.utime, and assert the reset is mtime + 2 h.
evidence: `return "parked", line, reset_time(line, tail[1])`; test line 97 constant `LIMIT = "Claude AI usage limit reached|1759140900"`; mutant M4 SURVIVED
